scope: Full exact source and all five complete expanded types/axiom reports for finite physical balanced-polynomial descent, with the two immediate balanced substitution modules read in full and prior sealed radial/spinor reviews reused.
evidence_category: Lean kernel-compiled finite polynomial evaluation identity and homogeneous-degree implication, under the explicit balanced-support hypothesis. No analytic invariance-to-support or infinite-series result is included.

findings.reason: A is ksRadialEven of ksBalancedPolynomialDescent P; B is ksRadialOdd of the same intermediate polynomial. Each is a genuine three-variable complex MvPolynomial. Both are the previously reviewed finite formulas, without a replacement chosen by existence.

The input four polynomial variables mean z0,z1,w0,w1. The intermediate four variables mean X0,X1,X2,r. The balanced quadratic substitution explicitly constructs this change using (r+X2)/2, (X0+iX1)/2, (X0-iX1)/2 and (r-X2)/2. Final A and B use only X0,X1,X2; sharing the Fin 4 index type does not silently identify the two input meanings.

For every actual supported exponent d, d0+d1=d2+d3 is explicit in both physical evaluation and homogeneous descent. No theorem here derives it from circle invariance, analyticity or a physical PDE. The assumption is not itself the requested A+rB identity.
Input homogeneity at degree 2m gives d0+d1+d2+d3=2m for every supported exponent. Together with balance, elementary natural arithmetic gives d0+d1=m. No half-degree statement is assumed.

The intermediate balanced quadratic polynomial is homogeneous of degree m. Applying the previously sealed radial homogeneity lemmas gives A homogeneous of degree m and B homogeneous of degree m-1. The m=0 clause separately proves B=0, avoiding misuse of truncated natural subtraction.

The left side evaluates P at exactly [ksSpinor y 0,ksSpinor y 1,star(ksSpinor y 0),star(ksSpinor y 1)]. The right side evaluates the same A and B at Complex.ofReal(ksMap y k), with multiplier Complex.ofReal(norm(y)^2). The actual real radial identity is cast into Complex and discharges the sole radial-reduction relation.

The physical identity is quantified over every real y in KSSpace, including y=0; it divides by no coordinate or radius. The evaluation theorem needs no homogeneity assumption and therefore applies to all finite balanced-support polynomials. Empty support, zero P and degree-zero constants are covered.

The five exact proof closures contain only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The definitions use noncomputable Mathlib complex polynomial operations; they specify algebraic objects but do not provide an executable rational-polynomial program or a bit-cost theorem.

trust.cache_disclosure: Existing pinned library/prior-audit object cache and newly compiled continuation objects reused; this is not a source dependency rebuild.

limitations: Homogeneity means support in the declared degree; zero outputs are permitted, and no nonzero or exact totalDegree equality is implied.
An invariant analytic function has not been converted into balanced polynomial support by this module.
No infinite sum, common complex convergence radius, analytic-plus-distance decomposition, uniqueness or compatibility of physical germs is asserted.
Coefficient L1 estimates and any finite D12 bound are separate from these five declarations.

The physical identity is established on the real KS slice with conjugate spinor variables. It does not assert equality for four arbitrary independent complex variables after the real radial substitution.
No executable rational-polynomial implementation, certified energy solver, termination, bit complexity or full Theorem T is established here.
The review reused existing compiler and strict-audit receipts and is not an isolated source-dependency rebuild.
